title: Flashed by devlab; the shell flash script retired
done: surya flashed from the pristine stock image by devlab flash and brought back by devlab provision, all 20 checks passing; flash.sh removed, as planned once devlab had done a real flash. A new check, root-fills-its-partition: the first boot had left the system at 2 GB on a 104 GB partition.
rejected: That: two ways to flash drift apart; the shell original stays in git history.

title: Both speakers heard - then withdrawn
done: With the author's EarPods as the lab's microphone, devlab hear played a 1000 Hz tone on each speaker and heard both: left at -24.0 dBFS, right at -29.2 dBFS, each over 70 dB above the silent room. The tones are in the manifest. Observed, not judged: the right read 5 dB quieter - the microphone's place or the speakers themselves; one measurement cannot say. WITHDRAWN the same day: the microphone was worn by the author and moved; neither the levels nor the 5 dB difference can be relied on.
rejected: That, on one measurement from one position.

title: The lab's idea, told for anyone
done: What this lab is - one particular phone, everything true of it written down, experiments that fall back by themselves - as a piece of writing for a reader who knows nothing of it.

title: The suspend crash found: a FastRPC helper attached at suspend
done: After the flash the audio DSP died on every suspend attempt (the attempts abort at once: the USB link cannot go idle). Found by experiment, one change at a time: not a first-boot effect (9 of 9 on the second boot), not the sensor proxy (15 of 15 without it), but hexagonrpcd's RootPD helper - 0 of 8 without it, and 0 of 9 on a clean boot with it masked, all 21 checks passing. Masked in the manifest, so every flash has it. The check's resume counter, which always said 0, rewritten in awk and checked against a boot with 24.
considered: A hand-made change the manifest lacked; a first-boot effect; the sensor proxy; a stream left open.
rejected: All four, each by its own measurement. The old 'rare' crash was the same one: there the helper died with the first crashes and stayed down.

title: What the ear heard is withdrawn
done: The microphone was the author's earphones, worn on his head: its distance from the phone changed as he moved. The levels measured, the difference seen between the two speakers, and the passes themselves cannot be relied on. The heard checks are out of the baseline and the lab's microphone is un-named until one is fixed in place; the tool stays, proven to work mechanically.
considered: Keeping the results with a caveat.
rejected: That: evidence from an instrument that moves is not evidence, and a later failure would have looked like the phone getting worse.

title: The USB link no longer flaps
done: Reported by the author: the phone kept reconnecting on his PC (26 USB disconnects in 5 minutes on the lab machine). On USB a suspend cannot complete, and the shell retried every 12 seconds, each attempt dropping the link. A small service holds a kernel wake lock while the port is connected to a host - independent of any shell - baked in by the manifest, with a check. Known before, never written down: it is now.
rejected: That: a fix inside one shell does not hold under another, or under none.
